### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/types`, touching **35** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/types/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**12** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via meta.publishItem (sdk, the route ledger binds it to POST /api/v1/meta/:type/:name/publish, selected by route anchor /:type/:name/publish), publishItem (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.publishItem, bound to POST /api/v1/meta/:type/:name/publish))_
- `content/docs/api/metadata-api.mdx`  _(via /:type/:name/publish (route, bridged from symbol createData — its route source's handler names it; bridged from symbol deleteData — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via /:type/:name/publish (route, bridged from symbol createData — its route source's handler names it; bridged from symbol deleteData — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/currency.mdx`  _(via /:object/import/jobs (route, bridged from symbol createData — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/import-mappings.mdx`  _(via /:object/import/jobs (route, bridged from symbol createData — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object), runtimeTypes (symbol, a field of const object AUTHORING_RULES))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via createData (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation), updateData (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via /:type/:name/publish (route, bridged from symbol createData — its route source's handler names it; bridged from symbol deleteData — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via createData (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation), deleteData (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation), updateData (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via /:object/import/jobs (route, bridged from symbol createData — its route source's handler names it), /import/jobs/:jobId/undo (route, bridged from symbol deleteData — its route source's handler names it))_

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ERR_SUMMARY_RECOMPUTE (literal, a string literal in a comment in SummaryRecomputeRefusal; a string literal in isSummaryRecomputeRefusal))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/types/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `updateData (4 routes)`
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **51** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8196881e7042f4e57543a6aaceffc1ab0ec89422` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8dbdbf50c8c2fbfd8b4f86d672218b171e40d86c` — the merge of head `6e86fff7454fe0bac0f614e5a9cdbb7bf564448c` into base `8196881e7042f4e57543a6aaceffc1ab0ec89422`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8dbdbf50c8c2fbfd8b4f86d672218b171e40d86c && git checkout 8dbdbf50c8c2fbfd8b4f86d672218b171e40d86c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8196881e7042f4e57543a6aaceffc1ab0ec89422 6e86fff7454fe0bac0f614e5a9cdbb7bf564448c && git checkout -B drift-repro 8196881e7042f4e57543a6aaceffc1ab0ec89422 && git merge --no-ff 6e86fff7454fe0bac0f614e5a9cdbb7bf564448c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8196881e7042f4e57543a6aaceffc1ab0ec89422
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8196881e7042f4e57543a6aaceffc1ab0ec89422` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fe13d22d05d92d0e45e3190c159d58f59bac9f70`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/data-model-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/data-model-rules.fix-lines.test.ts, packages/lint/src/data-model-rules.summary-rollup.test.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.object-writes.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.summary-rollup-publish-gate.test.ts, packages/rest/src/crud-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/stale-summary-answer.ts, packages/rest/src/data-write-summary-recompute-refused.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/data.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/data-write-summary-recompute-refused.test.ts, packages/types/src/index.ts, packages/types/src/summary-recompute-answer.ts, scripts/check-engine-double-contract.mjs, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json + packages/spec/src/data/aggregate-field-type-compatibility.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/spec/scripts/check-error-code-provenance.ts, packages/objectql/src/aggregate-field-type-door.ts, packages/objectql/src/summary-aggregate.ts, packages/objectql/src/summary-errors.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (insert/update/delete recompute throw sites, the aggregate door call), packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts (callData), packages/rest/src/error-response.ts, AGENTS.md (changeset level rule)

Dispatch rulings judged against the tree, not adopted: (1) refuse sum/avg over a non-numeric child at save and publish; (2) refuse a missing child too unless a legitimate authoring order needs it admitted; (3) fix the persisted-write 500 only through an answer the platform already publishes, no new code, member or shape; (4) no packages/spec edit.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each judged:

- `sum`/`avg` whose child field type the aggregate table refuses is now refused under `rollup/non-numeric-aggregand` at `os validate`, `os build`, `os lint` (gating registry entry `lintSummaryRollups`, `surfaces: CLI_AND_RUNTIME`, `runtimeTypes: ['object']`), at the active object save (422 `INVALID_METADATA`), at `publishMetaItem` and `publishPackageDrafts`, and the draft's `_diagnostics` reads `valid: false`. RIGHT, and it is ruling 1. The predicate is `isAggregateCompatibleWithFieldType(fn, childType)` from `@objectstack/spec/data`, the same call `aggregate-field-type-door.ts` makes on `engine.aggregate`, which `aggregateSummaryValue` (`summary-aggregate.ts`) calls on every recompute (`engine.ts` calls `assertAggregationFieldTypesAccepted` inside `aggregate`). So the numeric-type set matches what the recompute actually aggregates: `sum` admits `number, currency, rating, slider, progress, summary, boolean, toggle`; `avg` adds `percent`; `text`, option, reference, temporal, `formula`, `autonumber`, JSON-stored types are refused for both. The engine door's one extra refusal, a `multiple: true` declaration, falls only on types already outside both rows, so no pair is refused at one door and admitted at the other. `sum` over `percent` refused and `avg` over `percent` admitted is the table's own row, and the engine refuses the same pair after the commit: RIGHT, though the card's word "non-numeric" undersells it (the rule's message names the accepted set, so the author reads the real criterion).
- A child field whose declared type is not a `FieldType` member: the lint arm would refuse (the predicate answers false) where the engine door is silent (`DECLARED_FIELD_TYPES` guard). Unreachable past the object schema, which refuses the type first; noted, not a finding.
- Silence when the child object or child field does not resolve, and never on `count`: RIGHT, the table's own consumer tier ("cannot answer, do not block"), and the tier the retired `lintDataModel` arm already held.
- The `min`/`max` arm keeps `summaryRollupAnswerFitsColumn` (numeric or boolean child) and its message, and moves from `os lint`-only into the gating entry, so it now also gates `os validate`, `os build` and the runtime object door. RIGHT as a narrowing (the stored column cannot hold the answer), and declared BREAKING in the changeset; see ② for the one sentence that understates its reach.
- A missing `summaryOperations.object` stays admitted at every door. RIGHT under ruling 2's own exception: the dev measured `install-local --unmanaged` saving `crm_opportunity` (its `line_total` roll-up) one active save before `crm_opportunity_line_item`, and the CLI pass may lack a dependency package's child. The runtime door's snapshot is the live universe plus the batch's pending drafts (`runtime-authoring-gate.ts` `mergePendingDeclarations`), so a child present in another package IS judged, and a draft child in the same publish batch is judged with its parent (tested both ways). The differential (`lint/src/runtime-gate.ts`, #22118) charges a stored parent's finding only to the write that creates it, so a child write that turns a summed field into text is refused and a label-only parent re-save of a legacy violation is not: RIGHT, and tested.
- Half 2, the wire: `POST`/`PATCH`/`DELETE /api/v1/data/:object[/:id]` on `RestServer` (`crud-routes.ts`) and on the runtime dispatcher (`domains/data.ts` `callDataWrite`) answer 201/200 with the body the same write answers when every roll-up recomputes, plus the dropped-fields header the success path sets. RIGHT, and this is the answer ruling 3 asks for: `written` on `SummaryRecomputeError` is, at each of the three engine throw sites, exactly the value the engine returns on the success path (`rowHookContexts[0].result` or the batch outcomes for insert, `hookContext.result` for update and delete), and `createData`/`updateData`/`deleteData` run the same `omitInternalFieldsFromWriteResponse`, `byIdUpdateRecord`, null-readback probe, `withheldMentions` and `notice` code on it before building the same literal. No new error code, no new response member, no new status: RIGHT.
- Is `packages/types/src/summary-recompute-answer.ts` or `packages/rest/src/stale-summary-answer.ts` a new public answer shape on the wire? NO. The carrier is a non-enumerable property under `Symbol.for(...)`, which `JSON.stringify` omits and which `earnedAnswerOf` reads back only in-process; `stale-summary-answer.ts` writes no response, it hands the protocol's own result to the route's existing `res.status(201).json(result)` relay. They are internal carriers. What IS new is the package API of `@objectstack/types` (`SummaryRecomputeRefusal`, `isSummaryRecomputeRefusal`, `staleSummaryRefusalOrThrow`, `withEarnedAnswer`, `earnedAnswerOf`, `staleSummaryAnswerLines`) and of `@objectstack/lint` (`lintSummaryRollups`): additive exports, levelled in ②, not wire shapes.
- Comparison with the live readers: `seed-loader.ts` (`writeRecoveringSummary`) and `import-runner.ts` (`recoverSummaryStale`) both match the refusal by an inline `code === 'ERR_SUMMARY_RECOMPUTE'` comparison, no imported class and no local constant, and read `e.written` as the write's result; the seed loader logs the stale column at `error`. The PR's reading of the refusal is the same reading, and both callers are untouched: the protocol rethrows the same error instance with the same `code`, `failures` and `written`. RIGHT in substance; the one place the PR departs from that precedent is spelling the code as a `const` in `@objectstack/types`, and the tree's own gate refuses that departure (④, must-fix).
- Doors not changed (form submit, batch and `*ManyData`, `cloneData`, MCP `create_record`, `callData`'s ObjectQL fallback, which builds no carrier so the refusal propagates as before): disclosed; outside the card's three doors. See ③.
- `scripts/check-engine-double-contract.mjs`: `receiptReturnPos` now also reads a receipt returned through a same-function `const answer = { ... }`, mirroring `localWhereIdBindings` (same `ts.forEachChild` walk, same over-approximation into nested closures), with an A/B self-test pair (bound receipt with refusal reported as `shared`; without, reported with `refusal === null`). RIGHT: without it the by-id seam scan would lose `updateData`/`deleteData` once their literal moved into a const. `engine-double-contract.pinned.json` gains the new metadata-protocol test file's engine double (delete/findOne/update, 1 each): a ledger entry, not a change of contract.
- `rule-explanations.ts`: `os explain rollup/non-numeric-aggregand` now covers both arms and names the reach. RIGHT.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/28661-summary-rollup-aggregand-gate.md`: `@objectstack/lint` minor, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` minor, `@objectstack/types` minor, `@objectstack/rest` patch, `@objectstack/runtime` patch; BREAKING (narrowing) banner, ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, both declaration lines present.

Clause-②: no (narrowing), on the PR body and the changeset body; `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. Matches what ships: a value an author could write (`sum`/`avg` over a text child) is now refused.

Against AGENTS.md's level rule ("a kind takes at least minor on a package the diff moves, none takes patch; a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships patch"): `lint` and `metadata-protocol` carry the narrowing, minor is RIGHT. `rest` and `runtime` are non-protocol bug fixes, patch is RIGHT. `types` ships additive exports consumed by `rest`'s `/data` doors; its own CHANGELOG levelled the identical shape minor at 18.0.0 (`notNullRefusalSite` and siblings, "Clause-②: yes (widening: three additive exports ...)"), so minor follows the package's precedent; RIGHT. `Check Changeset` on the head: success.

One prose gap, should-fix: the "Now, at the doors" paragraph says the `min`/`max` arm "now also gates `os validate` and `os build`"; it also gates the runtime object save and publish door for the first time (the registry entry is `CLI_AND_RUNTIME`), which the BREAKING line should name since a Studio or REST author with a stored `max` over a `datetime` roll-up is refused at the next publish.

### ③ Boundary flags

- open_questions 1 (missing child `qsf_nope`, options A/B/C, dev recommends A): ANSWERED A for this PR. Ruling 2 admits a missing child when a legitimate authoring order needs it, and the dev measured one (`install-local --unmanaged`, 9 reds). The runtime door still judges a child present anywhere in the live universe or the same publish batch, so what stays admitted is exactly the not-yet-present child, which reads 0/null and fails nothing. B (refuse only where the full universe is known) would need a second rule id and door-specific reach, and the CLI pass cannot tell "not yet installed" from "in a dependency package", so even there the table's own tier says be silent. Left to the maintainer only if a non-gating advisory (C) is wanted later.
- open_questions 2 (other write doors still answer 500 after a landed write): ESCALATED as a follow-up card, not a finding against this PR. The card named POST/PATCH/DELETE on the data door and the order scoped half 2 to "the objectql / REST write path that surfaces `SummaryRecomputeError`"; the carrier is in place, so the follow-up is a wiring change per door. Nothing in this PR makes those doors worse.
- Dev flag "step 4 on head was taken on a boot with only `@objectstack/lint` at base": a measurement method, not a product flag; the REST and runtime tests on the head cover the path the gate now prevents from being stored.
- Docs-drift bot: two changed files yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/types/src/index.ts`); the four prose edits are 58 to 59 author-time rules in CLI transcripts. Prose faces, not reviewed.
- Check-runs on the head (gate verdicts): `Lint · docs & code guards` FAILURE, red gate `Error-code provenance guard` (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:error-code-provenance`): "`@objectstack/types` stamps 'ERR_SUMMARY_RECOMPUTE' (constdef) at packages/types/src/summary-recompute-answer.ts:37, not listed under its own owner key"; 51 other gates in the lane passed. `Lint & Repo Gates` FAILURE as the aggregator of that lane. Answered in ④ as the must-fix. Everything else completed is success or skipped; Test Core, Build Core, Type Check (workspace, consumer gates, UI) and Test UI were still in progress at the time of this record and are not read as green here.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, read against the published spec on `main`: `AGGREGATE_FIELD_TYPE_COMPATIBILITY` (`packages/spec/src/data/aggregate-field-type-compatibility.ts`) already declares `sum` and `avg` over the text family refused, the engine's aggregate door already refuses the pair on every recompute, and the roll-up never answered a value; the only thing the consumer lost is a 500 on every child write. The authoring door now makes the spec's own refusal real, at the door, in the spec's own words (accepted set named). No declared capability is taken away at the consumer. Half 2 answers an already-published answer (the write's own success body) and leaves the protocol-level refusal, the seed loader and the import runner as they were. The design holds on both halves; the tree does not.

Must-fix:

1. The head's own gate is red. `check:error-code-provenance` reads `const SUMMARY_RECOMPUTE_CODE = 'ERR_SUMMARY_RECOMPUTE'` in `packages/types/src/summary-recompute-answer.ts` as a stamp site of a registered code attributed to `@objectstack/types`, which has no owner-key row for it. The guard's two prescribed fixes (a row under the `@objectstack/types` owner key, or a `PROVENANCE_WAIVERS` entry) both live in `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`, which ruling 4 closes. The route that stays inside the rulings is the one the live tree already uses for this code: `seed-loader.ts` and `import-runner.ts` match it by an inline `code === 'ERR_SUMMARY_RECOMPUTE'` comparison with no constant, which is not a stamp pattern, and `@objectstack/types` emits nothing (it only recognises the engine's refusal). Drop the `const`, compare inline in `isSummaryRecomputeRefusal` (keeping the module header's note that the class lives in objectql and would cycle), type `SummaryRecomputeRefusal.code` as the literal, and let the lane go green on the next push. Until the gate answers success the head is refused on the check-runs alone.

Should-fix:

2. Changeset: name the runtime object save/publish door in the `min`/`max` sentence of the BREAKING paragraph (② above).
3. `staleSummaryAnswerLines` keeps `reportedStaleSummaries` for the life of the process, keyed child and parent.field, never cleared. After an operator fixes and republishes the field, a later recompute failure of the same column for a different reason (a driver fault after retries) is not said again by the door; the engine's own `warn` per failure still fires, so the operator is not blind, but the "reported once per field" promise is once per process, which the line could say.
4. Open question 2's follow-up card (form submit, batch and `*ManyData`, `cloneData`, MCP `create_record`), filed with the dedupe words the dev report gives.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c3e6ceb5265e3f35667450e03ee9a6864bcc1924`
Local-runs: probe — the provenance guard's three published STAMP_PATTERNS (objlit, assign, constdef) replayed over packages/types/src/summary-recompute-answer.ts at this head with comments masked, because the `Lint · docs & code guards` lane that carries the real `check:error-code-provenance` run was still in progress and the checkout here has no tsx to run the script itself
Scope: packages/types/src/summary-recompute-answer.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/data.ts + .changeset/28661-summary-rollup-aggregand-gate.md (prose face, read for ②), packages/spec/scripts/check-error-code-provenance.ts (STAMP_PATTERNS, comment masking), packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts (the objectql owner row), packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts and packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts (the inline-comparison precedent)

Delta of one commit over the FAIL record on fe13d22d; everything that record judged right stands unchanged, the three files above are the whole diff.

### ① Derived judgments

- Must-fix 1 answered. `const SUMMARY_RECOMPUTE_CODE` is gone; `isSummaryRecomputeRefusal` compares `code === 'ERR_SUMMARY_RECOMPUTE'` inline, the reading `seed-loader.ts` and `import-runner.ts` already use, and the module header now says the code is read here and stamped by objectql, whose owner key holds the ledger row (`@objectstack/objectql`, line 777 onwards of the ledger). The probe over the comment-masked file finds no objlit, assign or constdef site; the three remaining mentions are the inline comparison (not a pattern: the assign regex needs `=` then a quote, and `===` breaks it) and two comments, which the guard masks. RIGHT, and no packages/spec edit (ruling 4).
- The deviation, `readonly code: string` in place of the literal type: ACCEPTABLE.
